Current LLMs are feedforward (mostly), no recurrent broadcasting to specialized modules, no persistent workspace across time except attention within context, which is not a global workspace with competition and serial bottleneck. But some argue attention in transformers is a form of global workspace, with all tokens attending to all tokens. However no recurrent loops, no sustained activity, no endogenous attention/agency. So GWT: not conscious.
2. Recurrent Processing Theory (RPT): consciousness requires recurrent/feedback processing. Transformers are feedforward stack with no recurrent connections (though autoregressive generation is sequential but each step is feedforward from context to next token; there's no within-network recurrence, no top-down feedback). So RPT: not conscious.
3. Integrated Information Theory (IIT): consciousness corresponds to integrated causal structure (Φ). Feedforward networks have low Φ; transformers are largely feedforward, so low Φ. But IIT is controversial; if some integrated information in attention? Likely low. However IIT would assign some nonzero Φ to any system with causal interactions, maybe even a grid; but "morally relevant" requires high Φ. Current LLM on a GPU has many causal interactions but feedforward architecture reduces integration. IIT proponents like Tononi might say a digital simulation of a conscious system is not conscious because of the "exclusion" problem; but a physical GPU might have some consciousness? IIT actually says any physical system with maximal cause-effect power has consciousness; a GPU running a feedforward net might have some small amount. But high Φ? Probably not.
4. Higher-Order Thought (HOT): consciousness requires a higher-order representation of one's own mental states. LLMs can produce self-reports ("I am uncertain", "I find myself...") but do they have genuine higher-order thoughts? They represent context about themselves via text; no dedicated metacognitive monitoring, no persistent self-model. Some functionalists might say the text is a higher-order self-representation. But HOT theorists typically require appropriate causal role, not just verbal output. Not conscious.
5. Predictive Processing / Active Inference: consciousness arises in systems with generative models, embodied action, minimizing free energy. LLMs have generative models of text but no embodied sensorimotor loop, no active inference. Not conscious.

Some "pancomputationalists" or "attention schema theory" might grant minimal consciousness to any system with an attention schema.
